record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Is there any function whose best known or optimal algorithm really needs space s in the ordinary model SPACE(s), but can be computed using almost entirely catalytic memory in the sense of belonging to CSPACE(≪ s, ≈ s), with only a much smaller ordinary work tape and nearly all memory coming from restorable catalytic space?

evidence.quote: Definition 2. The class CSPACE(s, c) is the set of all functions which can be computed by a catalytic Turing Machine which has space s and catalytic space c.

Problem 10. Find any function whose optimal space algorithm can be made almost entirely catalytic, i.e. a function requiring—or even that we only know how to do in— SPACE(s) but which is computable in CSPACE(≪ s, ≈ s).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A catalytic Turing machine has, in addition to its input tape and an ordinary work tape of size s, a separate "catalytic" work tape of size c that is initialized with an arbitrary string τ ∈ {0,1}^c. The machine may read and write on the catalytic tape during computation, but at the end of computation the catalytic tape must be returned to its initial content τ, for every choice of τ. The class CSPACE(s, c) is defined as the set of all functions f computable in this model with ordinary work space at most s and catalytic space at most c. Let SPACE(s) denote the usual deterministic space-s class.

Problem. Exhibit any function f together with a parameter s = s(n) such that:
(i) the best known (or known optimal) algorithm for f in the ordinary model uses work space Θ(s); and
(ii) f ∈ CSPACE(s', c) where s' = o(s) (i.e., s' ≪ s, the ordinary work tape is asymptotically much smaller than s) and c = Θ(s) (i.e., the catalytic tape size is comparable to the original space bound).

In words: find any computational task whose ordinary-space algorithm can be converted into one in which almost all of the memory used is restorable catalytic memory, with only a much smaller residual ordinary work tape. Alternatively, prove no such function exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Catalytic space remains an active research area. Recent works (2024–2025) have resolved several structural questions about catalytic classes (e.g., CL = CNL, CL = CPrL, collapsing catalytic classes, quantum catalytic space), but no result is reported exhibiting a specific function whose best known ordinary-space algorithm can be made almost entirely catalytic in the sense described (small ordinary work tape, with nearly all space provided by restorable catalytic tape). The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Collapsing Catalytic Classes
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work has settled almost all questions regarding non-deterministic and randomized catalytic computation... CL=CNL ... CL=CPrL.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress focuses on structural collapses of catalytic classes, not on producing explicit almost-entirely-catalytic algorithms for ordinary-space functions.

status_evidence.title: Catalytic computing - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Understanding CL remains a major open problem, as TC^1 remains the most powerful containment to date.
status_evidence.claim: Core questions about the power of catalytic space relative to ordinary space remain open.

status_evidence.title: Almost-Catalytic Computation
status_evidence.snippet: Defines a relaxation where the catalytic tape is only restored on inputs from a specific catalytic set A.
status_evidence.claim: Related 'almost-catalytic' relaxations are studied, but do not resolve the specific problem of converting an optimal SPACE(s) algorithm into one in CSPACE(≪s, ≈s).
